claims.text: A minor Al addition to CrFeCoNi promotes preferential cation diffusion relative to Si or Mn additions.
Preferential diffusion induced by Al produces a continuous oxide scale containing primarily Cr2O3 and Al2O3.
The Cr2O3-Al2O3 composite scale has improved adhesion.
The Al-containing composite oxide grows slowly.
The Al-containing composite oxide relieves interfacial stresses.
The Al-containing scale resists cracking and spallation above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive environments.
Elevated-temperature exposure to a reactive environment causes oxide scales to form on alloys.
Differences in thermal-expansion coefficient between an oxide scale and its substrate can cause scale cracking and spallation during thermal cycling.
A coherent, dense Cr2O3-Al2O3 scale limits oxygen ingress.
A Cr2O3-Al2O3 scale minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch with the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
Al addition enhances the outward diffusion of both Al and Cr to the alloy surface.
Al and Cr selectively form passivating oxides in AlCoCrFeNi.
Compared with Si- or Mn-containing scales, the Al-containing mixed scale has slower growth and fewer defects because of better lattice matching and lower oxygen diffusivity.
Reduced oxide-scale defect formation relieves internal stresses that would otherwise cause spallation.
The Al-added alloy will exhibit fewer or smaller cracks and no significant spallation relative to the baseline and Si- or Mn-added alloys.
Si- or Mn-added CrFeCoNi alloys will form less-dense oxide layers prone to cracking or spallation.
External protective oxidation by an active element such as Al requires a critical solute concentration governed by the competing outward active-element flux and inward oxygen flux.
Alloy phase structure and processing conditions may affect the high-temperature oxidation result.
